newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Jews reassured after meeting Chirac.
newsitem.headline: French Jews reassured after meeting Chirac.

text.p: French Jewish leaders met President Jacques Chirac on Wednesday to discuss his tense recent visit to Israel and said afterwards they were reassured about the future of Franco-Israeli relations.

"He told us that his friendship for the (French) Jewish community had always existed and would continue to exist as would his friendship for the state of Israel and its prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, who, he said, was a true personal friend," community leader Jean Kahn told reporters.

The Jewish leaders called on Chirac in the wake of his controversial Middle East tour last week when he argued with Israeli guards in Jerusalem's Old City and called for a Palestinian state, an idea which is anathema to Israel's rightist government.
"We were told (by Chirac) that we could report to you that Franco-Israeli relations were good," Chief Rabbi Sitruk said.

Sitruk said he was pleasantly surprised by a new, relaxed tone between Israel and France. He said Chirac aides were on the telephone with Netanyahu advisers in Jerusalem when the group was ushered into the president's office.
